chunks: Three narrations: Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Regarding the man who is unconscious for days, he said, 'He does not make up anything of his prayer.'

Four: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said: I asked him about the one who is unconscious for a day or more, whether he makes up what missed of the prayer or not, so he wrote (in reply), peace be upon him: 'He does not make up the fast, nor does he make up the prayer.'
ai.seo_question: Does a person who is unconscious for days need to make up their missed prayers and fasts?
ai.summary: These narrations from the Tahdhib al-Ahkam clarify that prolonged unconsciousness (gha'bah) exempts the individual from both making up missed prayers (qada al-salat) and fasting (qada al-sawm), distinguishing this state from mere sleep or minor illness. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it relieves the burden of worship during periods where the mind is completely detached from accountability, reflecting the principle that the pen is lifted from the insane and the unconscious.
